sections.h2: Which offices deal with property tax in Sauk County, Wisconsin?
sections.html:
Your local assessor sets the value, your town, village or city treasurer takes the first payment, and the Sauk County Treasurer handles second installments and delinquent bills. The county office is in the West Square Building, 505 Broadway, Room 148, Baraboo, WI 53913. It is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and the phone number is 608-355-3275.

Assessment in Wisconsin happens at the municipal level. The Department of Revenue's Guide for Property Owners says the assessor of each taxation district determines the value of taxable property, so a Sauk County owner asks the local clerk, not the county, who the assessor is.

The county's Treasurer page also links to the Ascent Land Records System, where you can look up a parcel and pay second-installment and delinquent taxes online.

sections.h2: What kind of county is Sauk County for a home seller?
sections.html:
Sauk County is a mid-sized rural county of 849 square miles whose seat and largest city is Baraboo. It was created in 1840 and organized in 1844. Its other cities are Reedsburg and Wisconsin Dells, which is mostly in neighboring counties. The county sits in the Greater Madison area, and Baraboo anchors its own micropolitan area.

Visitor spending shows up in the numbers. Census data put accommodation and food service sales at about $818 million in 2022, roughly double Rock County's figure even though Sauk has less than half the population. County parks such as Lake Redstone, Man Mound and White Mound, plus the Great Sauk State Trail, add to the recreation pull. Ask the local clerk for the school district and municipality on your parcel, because those levies make up the bill.

sections.h2: When are Sauk County property taxes due?
sections.html:
The first installment or a full payment is due to your local treasurer by January 31, and the second installment is due to the County Treasurer by July 31. The county's Treasurer page spells out a rule that catches people: pay each installment on or before five working days after its due date, or the total unpaid balance becomes delinquent.

  • January 31: first installment or full payment, paid to the local treasurer.
  • July 31: second installment, paid to the Sauk County Treasurer.
  • After July 31: delinquent balances are collected by the County Treasurer.

Four towns allow the first installment to be paid online through the county's land records system, using the same fees as the county (listed below): Delton, Fairfield, Greenfield and Sumpter. In every other municipality, call your local treasurer for payment options.

  • Credit card: 2.50% of the payment.
  • Debit card: $2.95 flat per transaction.
  • Electronic check: $1.50 per transaction, up to $10,000.

Source: Sauk County Treasurer.

sections.h2: What does a late payment cost in Sauk County?
sections.html:
Delinquent balances accrue 1.5% in interest and penalty on the first of every month until paid in full. Because a missed installment makes the entire remaining balance delinquent, a small slip on the July payment can put the whole second half on the interest clock.

Mail timing needs care. The county notes that since August 2025 the Postal Service stamps postmarks at regional sorting centers, so a letter dropped in a mailbox may carry a date several days later. Many state tax deadlines turn on the postmark. The county advises taking the payment into a post office and asking the clerk to date stamp the envelope in front of you.

If you expect to pay late, call the County Treasurer at 608-355-3275 and ask for the exact payoff figure for the day you plan to pay.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Sauk County property assessment?
sections.html:
Go to the assessor first, then to your municipality's Board of Review if the value still looks wrong. Under s. 70.47 the board meets once a year during the 45 days that begin on the fourth Monday in April. The clerk of your town, village or city publishes the date and place, so check the notice or call the clerk's office in March or April.

  • Open book comes first. It is the informal period when the finished roll is open for review and the assessor is present.
  • Notify the clerk of your objection at least 48 hours before the first Board of Review meeting.
  • File the written objection form in the first two hours of that meeting. The board can waive the notice rule for good cause.
  • Object to the combined value of land and improvements, because Wisconsin does not allow an objection to only one of them.
  • After the board rules, the Department of Revenue takes appeals under s. 70.85 for a $100 filing fee, and circuit court review is available within 90 days.

The excessive assessment claim under s. 74.37 requires a prior Board of Review appeal and a written claim to the municipality by January 31 of the year the tax is payable.

sections.h2: What if I fall behind on Sauk County property tax?
sections.html:
Call the County Treasurer first, and keep every notice you receive. Delinquent interest builds on the first of each month, so the payoff figure changes depending on the day you pay. Ask for the amount in writing if a sale or refinance depends on it.

Owners with a mortgage escrow account should confirm with the lender that it is paying on time, and compare the annual escrow statement against the January 31 and July 31 dates above. A late lender payment still triggers the same interest.

The county's Treasurer page also lists the Wisconsin Help for Homeowners program, a state program for overdue housing bills. Ask the Treasurer or the program's call center, 1-855-2-HOME-WI, whether it is still taking applications before you count on it.

sections.h2: How does property tax affect selling a house in Sauk County?
sections.html:
Ask the County Treasurer for a payoff figure before you list or accept an offer, then tell the title company. If the first installment is paid and the second is open, the closing agent needs the unpaid amount and the interest to date. For a delinquent parcel the balance can include interest accrued month by month.

Sellers of one to four unit homes owe the buyer a completed real estate condition report. Section 709.01 exempts a court-appointed fiduciary who has never lived in the house, which often covers an estate sale after a death. Owners who did live there, and transfers that are not exempt from the real estate transfer fee, must complete the report.

Gather your last tax bill, any special assessment notices and permit records before you fill in the report. Section E of the statutory form asks about taxes, special assessments and permits.

A buyer who pays cash can shorten the timeline, but the tax balance and the disclosure duties are the same as in any other Sauk County sale.

faqs.q: Who collects Sauk County property tax?
faqs.a: Your local treasurer collects the first installment or full payment by January 31. The Sauk County Treasurer collects second installments due July 31 and all delinquent payments. The Treasurer's office is at 505 Broadway, Room 148, Baraboo.

faqs.q: How can I pay my Sauk County property tax online?
faqs.a: Use the Ascent Land Records System linked from the county Treasurer page for second-installment and delinquent taxes. The processor charges 2.50% on credit cards, $2.95 on debit cards and $1.50 on e-checks up to $10,000. The towns of Delton, Fairfield, Greenfield and Sumpter also accept first installments there.

faqs.q: What is the late fee on Sauk County property tax?
faqs.a: Delinquent balances accrue 1.5% interest and penalty on the first of each month until paid. An installment paid more than five working days after its due date makes the whole remaining balance delinquent.

faqs.q: Does the county set my Sauk County assessed value?
faqs.a: No. Wisconsin assessors work at the municipal level, so your town, village or city assessor sets the value. Appeals start with that assessor and then go to the municipal Board of Review, which meets in the 45 days after the fourth Monday in April.

faqs.q: Do I have to pay Sauk County property tax before I sell?
faqs.a: Any unpaid amount has to be settled at or before closing, and the County Treasurer can give you the balance. Share that figure with the title company so it comes out of the proceeds. You must also give the buyer a completed real estate condition report unless an exemption in Wisconsin chapter 709 applies.
